dateLabel: wood dated mid-1400s to 1800s; first reported 1864
title: Undeciphered: Rongorongo of Rapa Nui
summary: None of the Rongorongo glyphs can be read. Most specialists think it is proto-writing rather than full writing, and whether it was invented before European contact is still argued.
why: If home-grown, it would be one of very few independent inventions of writing in human history.
question: Is Rongorongo true writing, did it arise before European contact, and what does it say?
evidence: About 26 accepted texts survive; first documented 1864. A 2024 study dated one tablet's wood to the mid-1400s, but that dates the wood, not the writing.
wouldSettle: Securely dated pre-contact inscribed objects, or an internal decipherment that reads consistent Rapa Nui language.

theories.name: Proto-writing, not full script
theories.idea: The prevailing view: the glyphs were a memory aid rather than a full system recording spoken language.

theories.name: Inspired by the 1770 Spanish treaty
theories.idea: Some scholars suggest islanders created it after seeing Spaniards write during a 1770 treaty signing.

theories.name: Independent internal invention
theories.idea: Others see it as a development within Rapa Nui culture, not prompted by Europeans.
